headline: THE HISTORICAL BODIES ARE GONE AS BYTES BUT THEIR RECIPES SURVIVE; AND S027's 2.25 MIDPOINT IS A 2.98-EBPW BODY THAT NEVER GENERATED COHERENTLY

WHERE_THE_BODIES_WENT.mechanism: every historical body path in the receipts points inside a Grok worktree under ~/.claude-grok/worktrees/. All three are REAPED.
WHERE_THE_BODIES_WENT.precedent: this is the SAME failure that produced CLEAN_REBUILD_A: the 2.60 executable quoted as authority did not exist as bytes because its worktree was reaped. It was rebuilt from parent + recipe, and the rebuild proved the incumbent held NO unique weight bytes.
WHERE_THE_BODIES_WENT.consequence: RECONSTRUCTIBLE, not lost. The bf16 parent is on disk at 52 GB and the recipes are in the receipts, so rebuilding is from a RECEIPT, not from memory -- which is what S027 §0B permits when the original is truly gone.

receipt_says.THE_CORRECTION: 2.25 is the MLP BODY rate. The COMPLETE EXECUTABLE is 2.980 EBPW, which is LARGER than the 2.596957 clean rebuild. It is not a smaller midpoint at all. This is precisely the Variant-A discrepancy S027 §12 warns about, sitting inside S027 §0B.
receipt_says.generation_finding: Q2F g64 greedy-with-EOS emitted 2 tokens (' IR') then im_end. Forced 16-token sample judged VARIED, not coherent: ' IR<think>\n\nThe user is asking me to explain, in ordinary' with ids 15769, 248046, 248046, 248046, ...

S027_0B_CORRECTED_q2f.reconciling_27_55_ms: 27.55 ms IS real -- QWEN_COMPLETION_RECEIPT.json records 'COHERENCE=q2f_g64 2.25 bpw; EXECUTION=q2f_g64 27.55 ms'. It is a DIFFERENT measurement from the 33.09 tok/s whole-model decode. Both are true; they measure different things, and the steer fuses them into one body claim.
S027_0B_CORRECTED_q2f.what_2_25_actually_names: the MLP ORGAN coherence floor, which is a real and useful law. It is not a whole-model body. The AKB already demoted a sibling claim -- 'attention sets the representation floor' -- to architecture-specific for the same class of reason.

LANE_D_LARGELY_ALREADY_ANSWERED.question_it_asked: Where does the 1.25-bpw binary g64 body diverge from q2f on real activations, and what is the smallest protected island that restores coherent generation while staying faster than q2f (27.55 ms)?

THE_ANSWER_TO_WHAT_INFORMATION_WAS_MISSI.earliest_token_logit_divergence: generated token 0. binary emits 271 sixteen times; q2f emits a varied sample from 15769. Dead before any later token can recover.
THE_ANSWER_TO_WHAT_INFORMATION_WAS_MISSI.reading: S027 §6 asks for a SPARSE information set. The measured injury is UNIFORM -- 64 of 64 layers over threshold and all three MLP organs within 0.05 of each other. That is the physical reason no sparse island was found, and it is a MECHANISM, not a failure to search.

best_candidate_cost.reading: even 0.5% protection costs 1.2506 EBPW of tax, lands at 2.50 complete EBPW -- essentially the 2.60 body -- and STILL did not cohere.

what_this_DOES_NOT_ESTABLISH: That the q2f or binary bodies cannot be rebuilt. They can, from parent + recipe; that has NOT been attempted here.
That no sparse healing set exists. FOUR were tried. Uniform injury makes one unlikely, but 'unlikely given a uniform rel-L2 map' is not 'proven impossible'.
Any modern 43-case capability score for q2f or binary. Neither has been run under the current harness -- the bodies do not currently exist to run.
That 27.55 ms would reproduce today. It has not been re-measured.
recommendation: LANE C's premise needs revising before it is executed: rebuilding q2f yields a 2.98-EBPW body that historically emitted 2 tokens then stopped, so it is NOT a stronger resident candidate than the 2.60 body it was supposed to beat. The genuinely open question the ladder should ask is the ORGAN one -- 2.25 is an MLP floor -- combined with cheaper NON-MLP organs, rather than a uniform whole-model rate.
